title: Algorithm-assisted personalized risk communication to encourage flu vaccination in the USA: three randomized field trials
title_zh: 算法辅助的个性化风险沟通以鼓励美国流感疫苗接种：三项随机田野试验
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare to identify high-risk patients. Laboratory studies are mixed regarding patient attitudes towards AI use. Here we field-tested whether informing patients of their risk for influenza and its complications can serve as an effective behaviour-change intervention to increase vaccination, and whether disclosing AI use in the risk determination or providing personalized reasons for the algorithm’s prediction (a form of explainable AI) influence message effectiveness. We ran three preregistered randomized controlled trials with over 90,000 unique healthcare system patients in the USA (ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT04323137 , NCT05009251 and NCT05509283 ). Patients identified by a previously validated machine learning algorithm as being at high risk for influenza and related complications were randomized to be sent no message or one of several different messages encouraging influenza vaccination (the primary outcome). High-risk nudges increased vaccination: among patients informed of their high risk, vaccination was 1.1–1.4 percentage points (3.3–5.4%) higher than those simply reminded to get a vaccine, and 1.7–3.5 percentage points (3.3–14.7%) higher than non-messaged patients. Vaccination was similar across message arms that did versus did not disclose ‘algorithm’ involvement or its risk explanations, indicating that patients are neither averse to nor appreciative of algorithm use or explainability in this realistic health application. This work was partially funded by the National Institute on Aging of the National Institutes of Health under award number P30AG034532. Rosenbaum et al. show that targeted communications highlighting patients’ high-risk status increased influenza vaccination uptake. However, they did not find an additional effect of informing patients that a computer algorithm was used to identify their risk status.
abstract_zh: 人工智能（AI）在医疗保健中越来越多地用于识别高危患者。关于患者对AI使用态度的实验室研究结果不一。在此，我们通过田野试验测试告知患者流感及其并发症的风险是否能作为有效的行为改变干预措施来提高疫苗接种率，以及在风险判定中披露AI使用情况或提供算法预测的个性化理由（可解释AI的一种形式）是否会影响信息的有效性。我们在美国的医疗系统中对90,000多名独特患者进行了三项预先注册的随机对照试验（ClinicalTrials.gov标识符：NCT04323137、NCT05009251和NCT05509283）。由先前验证的机器学习算法识别为流感及相关并发症高危患者的患者被随机分配发送无消息或几种不同的鼓励流感疫苗接种的消息（主要结局）。告知高危患者其高危状态的提示增加了疫苗接种率：与仅被提醒接种疫苗的患者相比，疫苗接种率高出1.1–1.4个百分点（3.3–5.4%），与未收到消息的患者相比，高出1.7–3.5个百分点（3.3–14.7%）。在披露‘算法’参与或其风险解释的信息臂与未披露的信息臂之间，疫苗接种率相似，表明患者在这种现实的健康应用中并不抗拒也不感激算法的使用或可解释性。Rosenbaum等人表明，针对患者高危状态的有针对性沟通增加了流感疫苗接种率。然而，他们未发现告知患者计算机算法用于识别其风险状态的额外效应。
